bundles.evidenceText: a belief is rational then if and only if that belief is in accordance with the reason and evidence that's available to the believer
bundles.rationale: The move asserts that rationality consists in conformity to available reason and evidence and can diverge from truth. That proposition is compatible with either verdict on theistic belief, so no bridge receives contact and no polarity applies. The nearest competitor is support for the pro motion bridge, excluded because the excerpt never asserts that theistic belief fails this standard.

bundles.evidenceText: my theodicy provides a possible account but mere possibility doesn't imply high probability
bundles.rationale: The move argues by evil-God parity that a merely possible theodicy does not make the corresponding God-belief probable or rational. This supports the pro subsidiary bridge that merely possible theodicies do not make belief in an all-powerful, all-loving God rational; the proposition cannot remain true without making that bridge more credible. Pro-motion support is the nearest competitor but is excluded because the narrower theodicy bridge receives the exact contact.

bundles.evidenceText: most Christians let alone Muslims and Jews can't even agree on what's necessary for salvation
bundles.rationale: The move asserts that grave consequences depend on salvation while major religious communities cannot agree on the conditions required. This supports the pro subsidiary bridge concerning an all-loving God attaching grave consequences to conditions sincere people cannot reliably identify; the compatibility test passes because the asserted disagreement directly increases that bridge's credibility. Pro-motion support is excluded because the move contacts the narrower salvation-confusion proposition rather than the complete motion conclusion.

bundles.evidenceText: those of us not so made or made so that we cannot see the hoop we be eternally punished
bundles.rationale: The move asserts that an all-loving, all-powerful God imposes eternal punishment on people unable to discern a disputed salvific requirement. This supports the pro subsidiary salvation-confusion bridge, and the proposition cannot remain true without making that bridge more credible. Support for the pro central bridge is excluded because the excerpt specifically concerns inaccessible salvation conditions, not the central comparison with the cumulative positive case.

bundles.evidenceText: if God exists there is an intelligent Creator behind it all
bundles.rationale: The move asserts that unguided physical processes undermine trust in cognition, whereas an intelligent creator supplies a basis for trusting minds and the universe's intelligibility. This supports the con subsidiary reason bridge, and its proposition cannot remain true without increasing that bridge's credibility. Con-motion support is excluded because the excerpt advances only the stated rational-minds component, not the complete cumulative conclusion.

bundles.evidenceText: natural selection does not um directly select for True beliefs but rather for advantageous behaviors
bundles.rationale: The move asserts that unguided selection favors advantageous behavior rather than truth and contrasts this with God-guided evolution aimed at rational knowledge. This supports the con subsidiary bridge about naturalism undermining confidence in evolved minds while a creator grounds trust; the compatibility test therefore passes. Con-central support is excluded because the narrower rational-minds bridge captures the exact proposition without inheriting the other cumulative components.

bundles.evidenceText: the reason this fine-tuning argument points so powerfully towards the existence of God
bundles.rationale: The move asserts that extremely specific life-permitting physical conditions are effectively impossible by chance and instead indicate a superintellect. This supports the con subsidiary fine-tuning bridge, and the proposition cannot remain true without making intelligent design more credible relative to unguided chance. Con-central support is excluded because the excerpt contacts the specific cosmic-design component rather than the combined case from reason, design, morality, and responses to suffering.

bundles.evidenceText: objective moral law points us to the existence of God as the only good explanation
bundles.rationale: The move asserts that objective moral law requires explanation, is difficult to derive from an impersonal universe, and points to God. This supports the con subsidiary morality bridge, whose proposition is directly made more credible by the asserted grounding contrast. Con-central support is excluded because exact contact lies with the narrower objective-morality proposition, not the entire cumulative inference.

bundles.evidenceText: that's not an argument in favor of theism
bundles.rationale: The move asserts that undermining atheism does not itself favor theism, that atheism was improperly equated with naturalism, and that evolution need not favor costly false beliefs. This attacks the con subsidiary reason bridge by challenging necessary steps from unguided evolution to cognitive distrust and then to God; those assertions cannot remain true without reducing that bridge's credibility. Support for pro subsidiary 3 is excluded under the direct-attack rule because the expressed target is the con reason bridge.

bundles.evidenceText: evolution is not going to select for things that are false and inaccurate about the world because it's entirely costly
bundles.rationale: The move asserts that selection favors broadly accurate cognition because false and inaccurate representations are costly, even though cognition is imperfect. This attacks the con subsidiary reason bridge's premise that unguided evolution undermines confidence in truth-tracking; the compatibility test passes because the assertion directly lowers that premise's credibility. Support for pro subsidiary 3 is excluded because this is a direct attack on the stated con bridge rather than an independently framed positive route.

bundles.evidenceText: our minds are not the product of a nonrational unguided process
bundles.rationale: The move asserts that created minds are directed toward understanding truth, while evolutionary success need not consistently correlate with truth. This supports the con subsidiary reason bridge that a creator grounds trust in rational minds whereas unguided naturalism does not; the proposition cannot remain true without making that bridge more credible. Con-central support is excluded because no design, morality, or suffering component of the combined bridge is asserted.

bundles.evidenceText: you suffer from an equally irrational standpoint
bundles.rationale: The move asserts that appeals to God's mysterious and undisclosed reasons leave the theist with the same epistemic problem alleged against naturalism, so the comparison cannot favor God. This attacks the con subsidiary reason bridge, and the proposition cannot remain true without reducing the claimed creator-based advantage in cognitive trust. Support for pro subsidiary 3 is excluded because the move directly targets the con reason inference rather than separately developing the pro evolutionary bridge.

bundles.evidenceText: but I don't think it's a um it's a defeater
bundles.rationale: The move concedes that suffering is counterevidence but asserts that it does not defeat belief in an all-powerful, all-loving God because arguments are available in response. This attacks the pro subsidiary suffering bridge by denying its defeating force, and the proposition cannot remain true without making that bridge less credible. Support for the con central bridge is excluded under the direct-attack rule because the expressed target is the pro suffering inference.

bundles.evidenceText: I don't think an atheistic belief can affirm that instinct
bundles.rationale: The move asserts that Christianity can affirm the normative intuition that suffering makes the world other than it should be, whereas an atheistic universe of blind indifference cannot ground that affirmation. This supports the con subsidiary morality bridge's contrast between divine and impersonal grounding, and the proposition cannot remain true without increasing that bridge's credibility. Support for the con central suffering component is excluded because the move does not deny gratuitous suffering or offer a theodicy.

bundles.evidenceText: any weighing up of things must take into account God's resources of what he's able to do in an afterlife
bundles.rationale: The move asserts that evaluating earthly suffering must include an eternal future in which God can compensate suffering and remove its effects. This attacks the pro subsidiary suffering bridge by challenging the inference that apparently uncompensated suffering serves no greater good; the compatibility test passes because the asserted afterlife consideration directly limits that inference. Support for the con central bridge is excluded under the direct-attack rule because the move targets the pro suffering proposition.

bundles.evidenceText: God didn't just look on our suffering indifferently from on high but actually entered into our broken World
bundles.rationale: The move asserts that named theodicies are taken seriously and that the Christian God experienced suffering and offers sufferers companionship and strength. Those propositions can remain true even if pervasive apparently gratuitous suffering is improbable under an all-powerful, all-loving God, so no bridge receives exact contact and no polarity applies. The nearest competitor is attack on pro subsidiary 1, excluded because neither professional attention nor divine participation states or challenges a necessary premise showing that suffering serves a greater good.

bundles.evidenceText: very much explained for us being a social species
bundles.rationale: The move asserts that evolution in a social species explains care, sacrifice, religious motifs, and the moral intuitions associated with suffering. This supports pro subsidiary 3, which says evolutionary accounts of morality undercut the claim that moral experience identifies God; the proposition cannot remain true without making that bridge more credible. Attack on con subsidiary 3 is excluded because explaining moral intuitions does not itself deny objective obligations or their possible metaphysical grounding.

bundles.evidenceText: if God commands us to do things because they are good then the good obviously exists independent of God
bundles.rationale: The move presents the Euthyphro dilemma: goodness is either independent of God or reducible to arbitrary divine command rather than morality. This attacks the con subsidiary morality bridge by challenging the necessary inference that objective goodness is intelligibly grounded in God; the proposition cannot remain true without lowering that bridge's credibility. Support for pro subsidiary 3 is excluded because this is a direct attack on the con grounding bridge, not an evolutionary account of morality.

bundles.evidenceText: the moral standards that you're holding them up against are probably the moral standards that have historically resulted from the influence of the Bible
bundles.rationale: The move asserts that biblical influence historically produced Western moral standards concerning human value and dignity. That historical causal proposition can remain true whether or not objective obligations are metaphysically grounded in God, so no bridge receives exact contact and no polarity applies. The nearest competitor is support for con subsidiary 3, excluded because social influence by a doctrine is not the bridge's proposition about the grounding of objective morality.

bundles.evidenceText: God commands uh what he does not because it is good but because he is the good
bundles.rationale: The move asserts that goodness is neither external to God nor arbitrary command but is rooted in the nature of the creator as the ultimate source of goodness. This supports the con subsidiary morality bridge, and the proposition cannot remain true without making divine grounding of objective goodness more credible. Con-central support is excluded because the excerpt contacts only the narrower moral-grounding proposition, not the cumulative inference from all three positive arguments.

bundles.evidenceText: you are stuck with hea having to admit that morality exists independent of God or the morality isn't morality
bundles.rationale: The move asserts that identifying God with goodness merely restates the dilemma: morality is either independent of God or reduced to whatever God's nature dictates. This attacks the con subsidiary morality bridge by denying that the proposed divine grounding resolves the necessary grounding problem; the compatibility test passes because the assertion directly lowers that bridge's credibility. Support for pro subsidiary 3 is excluded because the move directly attacks the con moral-grounding inference rather than offering an evolutionary alternative.

bundles.evidenceText: we live in a time and an age where Evolution has made it very clear that if God exists he chose to use Evolution
bundles.rationale: The move asserts that biological complexity once made creation rationally plausible in the absence of a natural account, but evolution now supplies such an account. This supports pro subsidiary 3 by using an evolutionary alternative to undercut the inference from apparent biological design to a creator; the proposition cannot remain true without making that bridge more credible. Attack on con subsidiary 2 is excluded because biological evolution can explain organismal complexity while leaving the separate cosmic fine-tuning proposition unchanged.
